ateret-zekenim/1:_: And he should be done on Shabbat and his day, and he should be treated with the words of Moriah in the name of the Gemara and the next day in the day of the High School, and he shall not eat meat at night, and he shall not think that he is the main of the fruitful feasts
ateret-zekenim/2:_: A little in Torah. So wrote Mahari Weil from that which we learn in first chapter Rav Ashi was sitting before R' Kahana; he said why did the rabbis not come to the beit midrash etc.; he said they are busy with the Purim meal — we learn the Purim meal pushes aside Torah study; nevertheless since they expounded "this is Torah" — mitzvah to engage in Torah before the meal and it protects him that no mishap occur at the meal — end of his words.
ateret-zekenim/3:_: First and foremost, see the Gemara as a sign, and if you forget to say about the miracles in the Gemara when it comes to the Moon, it will make us as miracles and wonders as you have done to our forefathers and that in the days of Mordechai, and that we will be hidden in the midst of Heaven’s Word. And if you forget about the miracles completely, even though the back of Dovfel does not return as a model of siman of the B.C. in the Purim, the psalmist returns it to the U.S. sign, and see the above, siman of the U.S. and siman of the Gemara is a sign of siman:
biur-halacha/2:א: (א) A person is obligated etc. — one could ask how did Chazal obligate what is mentioned in Torah and Prophets in several places that intoxication is a great stumbling block; one could say because all miracles done for Israel in days of Ahasuerus were through feasting, for initially Vashti was removed through feasting and Esther came, and so the matter of Haman and his fall was through feasting, therefore the sages obligated to become intoxicated enough that the great miracle be remembered through wine drinking; nevertheless all this is for the mitzvah and not to prevent [Eliyahu Rabbah].
biur-halacha/2:ב: (ב) Until he does not know etc. — thus Meiri: a person must increase joy on this day in eating and drinking until he lacks nothing; nevertheless we are not commanded to become drunk and diminish ourselves from joy of mitzvah, for we were not commanded joy of frivolity and foolishness but joy of pleasure reaching love of the Blessed One and thanks for miracles He did for us — see there what he explains gemara words. Thus Chayei Adam: since the entire miracle was through wine, therefore sages obligated intoxication and at least to drink more than usual to remember the great miracle; indeed one who knows about himself he will treat a mitzvah lightly in Grace after Meals or will not pray Minchah or Maariv or will behave lightly — better he not become drunk and all his actions for the sake of the mitzvah — end of his words.
biur-halacha/4:א: (א) It must be sent to the Levites, and so on, that the Gemara has proven from Jerusalem that it sends to the rich nothing less than it does not come out of it by shipping the dishes, and it means that in a single sage in the final. It is true that P did not mention this and it is appropriate to be careful about it:
biur-halacha/4:ב: (ב) Or kinds of foods etc. — in Turei Even he is in doubt if he sent two portions to one poor person whether he can count them for two to fulfill mishloach manot, for the poor too is included in ish lere'ehu, and to fulfill matanot laevyonim; if he gave another gift to one poor person did he fulfill or not — Gra brought this in his chiddushim. Peri Chadash wrote city of doubt surrounded — send the portions on the 14th which is for most of the world; see Peri Megadim who doubts this.

chatam-sofer/3:_: (there in Hagahah) and if he sends. NB see these laws what Peri Chadash wrote and in responsa ch. same Orach Chayyim siman 196 [there he wrote on Peri Chadash's words who doubted Rama who ruled if he sent portions to his friend and he did not want to receive, since he forgave him he fulfills; Peri Chadash wrote I do not know from where this is. Behold in Korban Netanel first chapter of Megillah he answered Peri Chadash from gemara Nedarim daf 63b that one can permit his vow not through a sage by saying behold I am as if I was accepted — the same here likewise, and they justified Rama's words. I say the gaon did not see what Ran wrote in name of Yerushalmi there 24a that it refers to stam and R' Meir and rabbis dispute whether giver's intent is for his own honor or recipient's honor, but if giver's intent is for his own honor it does not help by saying behold I am as accepted; if so Peri Chadash wrote well from where for Rama, for intent of mishloach manot instituters was for sender's need or for whom it was sent. I saw two reasons in Tosafos Yom Tov: wrote so there be profit for feast hosts perhaps his meal will not suffice, behold his friend helps him — see there; one could say even if he has much, nevertheless they instituted thus not to shame one who lacks as we say at end of tractate Taanit; if so as if he truly lacks enough his forgiveness is nothing; if he has anyway he should not forgive because of not shaming. But in Sefer Manot HaLevi it is written to increase peace and friendship — opposite narrow mitzvah scattered and divided etc.; if so one could say since he sent and showed affection he already fulfilled even though this one forgives — Peri Chadash wrote well from where for Mahari Weil and Rama to decide this. See there further law whether a woman is obligated in mishloach manot like a man, and see there what he wrote on Peri Chadash's words].
chokhmat-shlomo/2:_: Seif 2: a person must become intoxicated on Purim until he does not know between cursed is Haman and blessed is Mordechai. NB see what I wrote to explain this in my works on Orach Chayyim year 549 letter 224 and in derush for parashat Zachor year 553 in chiddushei Kehillat Yaakov — see there wondrous explanation with God's help; examine.
chokhmat-shlomo/3:_: (there seif 4) he must send his friend two portions etc. NB I was in doubt regarding mishloach manot: if he sends a sick person something forbidden that is permitted for him to eat, such as stam yayinam for a patient without danger, or another d'rabbanan prohibition, or a Torah prohibition for a dangerously ill patient — whether he fulfills mishloach manot if we follow the recipient and behold it is fit for eating, or we follow the giver and for him it is not fit. This can be resolved from the verse itself from what is written "and sending of portions ish lere'ehu" — the word ish is extra and it would suffice "and sending portions lere'ehu", and as Ezra wrote "and they sent portions to one not his friend"; since it says ish lere'ehu necessarily intent is portions ish fit for this one he sends to his friend, but what is not fit for him also for his friend he does not fulfill. Yet one could doubt: if both are sick and permitted to eat forbidden things and the sender has one permitted portion and one forbidden and his friend has nothing — if he sends the permitted to his friend he must eat the forbidden — what shall he do? In general certainly we say your life takes precedence and he eats the permitted and gives his friend the forbidden, for my question is in mishloach manot on Purim since I raised that mishloach manot sender must send what is fit for him — do we say if he eats the permitted then the forbidden is not fit for him since he has permitted, then he does not fulfill mishloach manot, and since in the end the forbidden will be eaten, better he eat the forbidden and send the permitted to his friend and fulfill mishloach manot; or do we say in any case your life takes precedence and he eats the permitted even though he does not fulfill mishloach manot — like this case Rava needs, requires study, examine well. (there seif 4 in Hagahah) and if he sends portions to his friend and he does not wish to receive or forgives — he does not fulfill etc. NB see in my works on Orach Chayyim year 561 in responsum to Krakow community who bought place in Laws of Yom Kippur siman 218 what he wrote on this matter relevant here — see there and examine.

shaarei-teshuvah/1:_: (א) In Shulchan Aruch: mitzvah to increase etc.; see Birkei Yosef in name of one kadosh in responsum: if Purim feast without bread he fulfilled; see Mahari Molcho: one who ate Purim night and meal continued till day and ate some by day fulfilled; see Kaf HaChayyim and Peri Chadash: at night even torch opposite him didn't fulfill; Beit Yosef "like night without torch opposite" means also by day in dark house, but not dark — plainly no lighting needed — lamp in daylight what help? I saw chasidim and men of deed at meal after Minchah lit candles to rejoice till end Bnei Chiya; see Likutei Peri Chadash Terumat HaDeshen s.k. 100: feast by day lights torch for joy and Yom Tov — see there; I didn't find in Terumat HaDeshen; see Mishna Berurah on Sefer Shoneh Halachot; Mor Uktzia: no need to remember Jerusalem destruction at Purim feast since must become intoxicated etc.
shaarei-teshuvah/2:_: and sleep. Avodat HaTumah; see in Siddur Amudei Shamayim who wrote his father the gaon in his youth practiced to fulfill the statement literally. One weak by nature (or who becomes foolish until he may come through this to improper act or words) should not drink more than enough, and proof to the matter Ribi"a — examine end of his words. His intent in what he wrote Ribi"a is acronym R' Yehudah bar Ilai, meaning R' Yehudah bar Ilai said in Yerushalmi he drinks only from Pesach to Pesach and girds his temples etc. — implies on Purim he did not drink since his drinking harmed his bodily health.
yad-ephraim/1:_: In the midst of Heaven’s Word, Heaven’s promise is that it is a blessing that Heaven’s glory is in the presence of Heaven’s glory, and that it is a great time before He is revealed to him, and that Heaven does not mean this:
yad-ephraim/2:_: In Magen Avraham s.k. 4; see beginning siman 570 we do not hold so as should read, and see there one may annul his vow; for Rambam it does not apply at all.
yad-ephraim/3:_: In Taz s.k. 1 a person must become intoxicated etc. Many wish to answer and explain what the intent is here etc.; to me the younger it was explained in a night vision that the intent is the main obligation of the feast is he be steeped in joy as written "and wine gladdens a person's heart", and because he be steeped in joy the joy of the Blessed One is his strength and he gives thanks and hallel to the Blessed One for the miracle from breadth of heart, per what they said gather wine etc.; therefore he should not become drunk more than enough that his mind be confused and he not recognize the force of the miracle at all; thus he said a person must become intoxicated on Purim until he does not know etc. — this "until" is and not "until" in general, meaning great is obligation of drinking here to become intoxicated until the boundary he does not know etc.; from this boundary onward it is nullification of intent of obligation the sages obligated to become intoxicated in order to give hallel and thanks, for since his mind is so confused he does not know between cursed is Haman etc. — clearly he has no mind and understanding to praise and glorify the force of the miracle; I considered it in the morning and saw it is correct and settled what gemara relied on the incident of Rabbah and R' Zeira who made Purim meal together etc., which superficially is an act to contradict; some poskim wrote the intent is from this one learns the halacha is not like Rava here; per what is written one could say on the contrary it brings support, for what they obligated days of feasting and joy has a boundary not to become drunk more than enough, for we precede Rabbah and R' Zeira etc.; and since they did not guard from crossing the boundary the matter came to danger — therefore one must be careful not to become intoxicated only until this boundary he does not know etc. and not cross.
